primary_source.paper: Shojaee, Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Horton, Bengio, Farajtabar, "The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity"

trace_source.checker_jumping: NOT in the Apple paper (it has no CJ qualitative-example trace, only a rule description + prescribed-algorithm text). Used instead: Song, Yue, Zhang, "Thinking Isn't an Illusion", arXiv:2507.17699 (2025), official repo github.com/magiclinux/thinking_is_not_an_illusion @ 1075515f839f21d67543d5193a8c95a2bc2b0564, notebook Scratchpad/DeepSeek/R1/DeepSeekR1_Scratchpad_Checker_Jumping.ipynb (all cell outputs) -- saved verbatim to published_trace_checker_jumping.txt. format_description.checker_jumping: Tool-augmented 'scratchpad' harness: each round the model returns JSON {"moves": [[color,from,to],...], "scratchpad": "state = [...]", "finished": bool}; state is a Python-list-literal string of the full board, refreshed once per ROUND (a harness-chosen batch of 1-7 moves), not once per individual move.
format_description.river_crossing: Free-form <think> CoT; the model spontaneously (not instructed to) interleaves prose with lines of the form 'Move k: [people] cross L->R/R->L' followed by 'State after Move k: a1: R, a2: L, A1: R, A2: L, boat on Right', ending in a final 'moves = [[...], ...]' answer line.

state_bits.checker_jumping: log2(C(2N+1,N)) board-arrangements upper bound; N=3 (board len 7): log2(35)=5.13 bits; growth with N is the knob, not depth
state_bits.river_crossing: 2N+1 bits upper bound (bank of each of 2N people + boat side); N=2: 5 bits; legal (safety-respecting) states are a small fraction of this

theory_citation: General propositional STRIPS plan existence is PSPACE-complete (Bylander, 1994, 'The computational complexity of propositional STRIPS planning', Artificial Intelligence 69). Neither puzzle family is given a complexity-class label in Shojaee et al. 2025 itself. The generalized river-crossing / jealous-husbands family admits known polynomial closed-form constructive solutions for fixed boat-capacity rules (Efimova, 2018, 'River Crossing Problems: Algebraic Approach', arXiv:1802.09369); checker/peg jumping (frogs-and-toads) admits a known greedy O(N^2)-move constructive solution, consistent with Shojaee et al.'s own (N+1)^2-1 minimum-move formula (Sec. 3.1). So plan EXISTENCE and one constructive plan are polynomial for these specific rule sets, but the paper evaluates whether an LLM finds/verifies a full valid sequence, which is not itself assigned a class here -- hence 'unclear' rather than asserting P-completeness or TC0.

notes: This desk.json describes BOTH sub-puzzles AS ORIGINALLY PUBLISHED (planning: model emits a full move sequence; a simulator validates it), per AMENDMENT 2 -- NOT our library's future tracking-formulation redesign (that was scoped in SOURCING.md/the phase-1 desk.json, now superseded in spirit though still relevant background). Fields that differ by sub-puzzle are nested as {"checker_jumping": ..., "river_crossing": ...} under the exact schema key; fields with one shared answer are given flat. Two real published traces were found (published_trace_checker_jumping.txt, published_trace_river_crossing.txt); tokens_per_step/tokens_total were measured with real tokenizer.json files pulled via huggingface_hub for Qwen/Qwen2-7B (ungated), NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B (ungated Llama-3 mirror; meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B is gated with no HF token in this environment), and unsloth/gemma-2-2b (ungated Gemma-2 mirror; google/gemma-2-2b is gated) -- no hand-estimates. steps_in_trace counts model-response rounds (CJ) or explicitly-labeled Move/State lines in the accepted solution path (RC); RC's full trace also contains ~4 abandoned attempts with their own reused 'Move 1/2/3' labels before the accepted path, which is why local_redundancy=low, prompt_recomputable=false, and interp_tractable=false for RC specifically -- the true next move is not visible in the prompt and requires backtracking search, and an interpretability probe would have to first disambiguate which 'Move 1' belongs to the eventually-accepted branch. Checker Jumping's JSON-scratchpad format is comparatively clean (interp_tractable=true) but was imposed by the harness's tool-augmentation prompt rather than emitted unprompted (format_natural=false), whereas River Crossing's 'State after Move k' annotation was volunteered by the model without being asked for it (format_natural=true) -- worth flagging since it argues the model finds narrating boat/bank state genuinely useful for this puzzle, unprompted. contamination_risk=medium (not low) because both puzzle families (missionaries-and-cannibals / jealous-husbands; frogs-and-toads / checker-jumping) are extremely well-known recreational-math and intro-AI-course puzzles, likely present verbatim in pretraining data for small N and the classic 3-couple/simple form -- though Apple's specific N-generalized a_i/A_i notation and R/B/_ board notation, run at larger N, are less likely to appear verbatim online. state_atomic_tokens=false confirmed by direct tokenization: quoted board symbols like "'R'" split into 2-3 tokens (quote-fused) and actor/agent ids like 'a1'/'A1' split into 2 tokens (letter+digit) on all three tested tokenizers. theory_class left 'unclear' rather than forcing solvable/TC0, NC1-hard, or P-complete: the underlying puzzle families have known polynomial constructive solutions (see theory_citation) but the paper does not classify the LLM-facing plan-verification task itself, and general STRIPS planning is PSPACE-complete.
